primary.title: RV565: Cross-Layer Co-Design for Frame-Independent Video Playback on MicroPython-Class ESP32-S3 Systems
primary.snippet: arXiv:2610.35935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Video on SPI-attached microcontroller displays is limited less by decoding than by where each byte lives and which stages run serially. We present RV565, a decode framework for frame-independent video whose decoded representation is the panel's native RGB565 format, and evaluate it on an ESP32-S3 with two ten-second windows of an openly licensed film. A serial path - inflate, then scale into internal-memory stripes overlapped with SPI direct-memory-access (DMA) transfers - meets the 41.7 ms deadline on the lighter window but misses all 7,200 frames of the heavier one. RV565's dual-core pipeline inflates the next frame on the second core during the transfer and sustains 24 FPS with zero misses and 10.3 ms of slack on both windows; frame time then equals the display transfer, which runs at 98.1% of the 40 MHz wire-time bound. primary.title: SLICE-CiM: Selective Layer-wise Inference Control Engine with Confidence-Based Early Exit for SRAM based Digital Compute-in-Memory
primary.snippet: arXiv:2610.37601v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Digital SRAM compute-in-memory (CIM) macros enable energy-efficient CNN inference by eliminating off-chip weight transfers; however, peripheral control logic introduces three inefficiencies: bit- slice over-activation at reduced precision (L1), unnecessary accumula- tion depth (L2), and idle precision-transition stalls (L3). To address these, we present four synthesizable peripheral blocks: a Flush-Merge Enable (FME) controller, a Confidence-Based Early-Exit (EE) module, a Precision Register with Decoder (PR/PD), and a Bit-Serial Cycle Controller (CC), co-designed to minimize switching activity, wordline overhead, and leakage. Implemented in TSMC 65-nm CMOS at 335 MHz, the peripheral framework occupies 1769.760 {\mu}m2 post-synthesis and 1982.131 {\mu}m2 post-PnR. primary.title: How Much Can Semiconductor Models Hide?
primary.snippet: Key Takeaways: Advanced packaging pushes process behavior across company lines, so what one supplier hides now shapes another company’s prediction. Encryption and abstraction protect the recipe cleanly, but neither tells the receiving engineer where the model stops being valid. A model can be accurate and still be wrong for the question asked, making its envelope as much a deliverable as the model. The goal seems simple — share the model without sharing the process. A materials supplier shouldn’t have to reveal a proprietary formulation just so a customer can predict how it will behave in a package, and a foundry shouldn’t have to hand over its recipe to provide a useful model of a chiplet. But advanced packaging is making that separation much harder to maintain. primary.title: Adapting DNNs to Embrace Voltage Scaling Induced Errors via Accumulation-Aware Quantization
primary.snippet: arXiv:2610.33824v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The pervasive deployment of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) across the computing spectrum has brought growing attention to energy efficiency, alongside raw performance. While voltage scaling is a potent knob for power reduction, its application in next-generation nodes is hampered by severe throughput degradation and susceptibility to process variation. This work aims to address these energy-reliability trade-offs by introducing a hardware-software co-design methodology, based on the observation that timing-robust bit ranges within the accumulator of a systolic array vary significantly across different voltage-frequency operating points. primary.title: RFChipAgent: Multi-Agentic AI Flow for Analog/RF Chip Design
primary.snippet: Analog/RF circuits remain the critical interface between digital computation and the physical world, and emerging standards from Wi-Fi 7 to 6G place stringent demands on them, yet analog/RF design remains one of the most labor-intensive steps in chip development. We present RFChipAgent, a first-of-its-kind multi-agent flow of large language model (LLM) agents for end-to-end analog/RF circuit design automation, in which AI agents collaboratively orchestrate the complete design flow under human supervision. RFChipAgent is built around four technical pillars. First, a multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) subsystem with private per-document FAISS indexing extracts design knowledge from existing engineering documentation. science.title: Fast 3D imaging reveals how seizures move through the brain
science.snippet: Neuroscientists are debating a seemingly simple question: which way does a seizure propagate in the brain? Answering such a question could advance our understanding of epilepsy, but requires the development of cutting-edge microscopy techniques that are far from simple. Researchers from the University of Georgia have now developed an improved light-sheet microscope with the ability to perform fast 3D imaging of zebrafish seizures. Reporting their findings in Biomedical Optics Express , the researchers found that seizures originated in the hindbrain and propagated forward (anteriorly). Here we present a frequency-tunable magnetic clocking concept based on the recurring translational motion of SAF skyrmions and define the material conditions needed to realize it in a Pt/Co/Ru/Pt/Co multilayer. Using micromagnetic simulations, we investigate the combined effects of interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and interlayer Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida exchange coupling, delineating the parameter space in which coupled N\'eel-type skyrmions with opposite topological charges form a stable, topologically compensated pair. science.title: Unification of Gravity and Standard Model: Weyl-Dirac-Born-Infeld action
science.snippet: arXiv:2508.10959v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a unified (quantum) description, by the gauge principle, of gravity and Standard Model (SM), that generalises the Dirac-Born-Infeld action to the SM and Weyl geometry, hereafter called Weyl-Dirac-Born-Infeld action (WDBI). The theory is formulated in $d =4-2\epsilon$ dimensions. The WDBI action is a general gauge theory of SM and Weyl group (of dilatations and Poincar\'e symmetry), in the Weyl gauge covariant (metric!) formulation of Weyl geometry. The theory is SM and Weyl gauge invariant in $d=4-2\epsilon$ dimensions and there is no Weyl anomaly. science.title: A gaussian-process reconstruction of gravitational-wave friction from dark standard sirens
science.snippet: arXiv:2610.36087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Standard sirens provide a direct probe of the cosmic distance-redshift relation and therefore a powerful test of whether gravitational waves (GWs) propagate as predicted by general relativity on cosmological scales. In many extensions of general relativity, GW propagation is modified by an anomalous friction term, which alters the amplitude evolution and leads to a GW luminosity distance that differs from its electromagnetic counterpart. In this work, we develop a non-parametric reconstruction of this anomalous friction from dark standard sirens. reserve.title: Hardware-Matched Spiking Neural Networks for Real-Time Purkinje Cell Spike Classification
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.37104v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distinguishing Purkinje cell (PC) simple spikes (SSs) from complex spikes (CSs) is key to studying cerebellar function. PC recordings commonly rely on wired headstages, whose tethers restrict natural movement in freely behaving animals. Untethered headstages remove this constraint, but cannot continuously transmit raw recordings within their power budgets, making on-headstage spike classification an attractive form of compression, provided it runs accurately in real time on constrained hardware. This work presents two compact spiking neural networks (SNNs) matched to their target hardware: ConvSNN, which maps to the Matrix Vector Processor (MVP) of an EFM32PG28 microcontroller, and StreamSNN, which processes one waveform value per timestep using learned time constants and fixed synaptic delays for a dedicated SKY130 circuit. reserve.title: Serotonin signaling enhances phagocytosis by brain macrophages through Htr2b and alleviates brain injury after stroke
reserve.snippet: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02482-y The serotonin receptor Htr2b activation enhances lysosome biogenesis and phagocytic clearance of debris to mitigate neuroinflammation and brain injury after stroke. The study proposes a potential monocyte-derived macrophage-targeted immune therapy to improve neurological outcomes after ischemic stroke.

reserve.title: Dual Strategy of Electroless Metal Deposition and Surface Silylation Toward Scalable Low-Temperature Hybrid Bonding for Advanced Packaging Applications
reserve.snippet: The growing demand for high-performance computing and compact electronics has driven the transition toward advanced three-dimensional (3D) packaging technologies. Traditional packaging technologies, such as micro-bump interconnections, face limitations in achieving sub-micrometer pitches, prompting the development of alternative bonding strategies. Among them, Cu/SiO2 hybrid bonding (HB) has emerged as a promising method for enabling fine-pitch, high-density interconnects in next-generation semiconductor packaging. In this study, a reliable low-temperature Cu/SiO2 HB process was developed by combining metal electroless deposition (ELD) on sub-micron pitch Cu pads with selective surface functionalization of the SiO2 dielectric layer using silane. reserve.title: Improved Gauge Conditions for Large Expansion Cosmological Models
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36123v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study develops a new gauge condition for performing long duration numerical evolutions of Einstein's equation on cosmological spacetimes with non-trivial spatial topologies. This new gauge makes it possible to perform reliable numerical evolutions on these manifolds in which the spatial volumes become more than one million times larger. This new condition was tested for this study by evolving homogeneous and isotropic initial data on exemplar manifolds with three spatial topologies: Sixth-Turn space, the lens space L(5,2), and the Seifert fiber space SFS[S2:(2,1)(2,1)(2,-1)].

reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36728v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gravitational-wave (GW) observations of binary black holes provide a powerful probe of general relativity (GR) in the strong-field regime. In effective field theory (EFT) extensions of GR, higher-curvature operators modify the binary dynamics and introduce corrections to the inspiral phase. reserve.title: Impact of deformation parameters on the greybody factor and Joule-Thomson expansions of Schwarzschild-AdS black hole
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the greybody factor and Joule-Thomson expansion of deformed Schwarzschild-AdS black hole models. We constructed the Klein-Gordon equation into a Schr\"odinger-like wave equation using tortoise coordinates and derived the exact effective potential. Also, we analyzed its behavior under varying physical parameters, including deformation parameters, mass and angular momentum. In this case, our results illustrate that increasing the deformation parameter enhances the effective potential, significantly impacting the absorption and scattering of massless scalar fields. reserve.title: Primordial black holes from a type-IIB/F theory inflaton potential
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36863v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the possibility of the formation of primordial black holes (PBHs) using an inflaton potential constructed by stabilizing all K\"{a}hler moduli employing both the perturbative and non-perturbative corrections in the large volume scenario in type-IIB/F string theory. We further introduce a small perturbation in one of the K\"{a}hler moduli that modifies the existing potential in the field space. The effective correction in the moduli space is made by introducing a localised Gaussian bump, which induces an ultra-slow-roll feature in the inflaton potential during the early cosmological inflation. reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate a description of self-gravitating Schr\"odinger--Poisson (SP) solitons in curved spacetime using a local inertial frame centered on the soliton. In the weak-field and non-relativistic regime, the effect of the background spacetime is incorporated into the SP equations through an effective tidal potential determined by the spacetime curvature. We apply this framework to a soliton moving along a circular equatorial geodesic around a Kerr black hole. The tidal field contains stationary and time-dependent quadrupolar components, which induce a deformation of the soliton and an associated mass quadrupole moment. reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.37331v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we investigate the geodesic dynamics and tidal force effects in neutral and electrically charged regular spacetimes inspired by T-duality. reserve.title: One Method to Find Them All: Analytic Black Holes beyond Einstein
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.37515v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rotating black holes offer powerful probes of gravity, but constructing their geometries beyond vacuum general relativity remains challenging. reserve.title: Gravitational wave signatures of periodic orbits around a Schwarzschild-like black hole
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.37525v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate how deviations from the Schwarzschild geometry affect the motion of massive test particles and the gravitational radiation associated with their periodic trajectories around a new improved Schwarzschild black hole. Periodic configurations are determined by examining the commensurability of the radial and azimuthal orbital frequencies. reserve.title: Weighing dark matter particles with gravitational waves
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.37638v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is commonly assumed that the mass of dark matter particles cannot be determined from their gravitational effects when dark matter behaves as collisionless matter. Here we show that extreme-mass-ratio inspirals observable by millihertz gravitational-wave observatories such as the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) could measure the mass of ultralight dark matter particles in sufficiently dense dark matter spikes. The separation of scales between the two black holes allows ultralight dark matter to form a collisionless density spike around the massive primary while retaining wave effects in its interaction with the stellar-mass companion. reserve.title: How particle physics stops ultra-relativistic bubbles and shapes their gravitational waves
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36160v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The gravitational-wave spectrum produced by ultra-relativistic bubbles in a first-order cosmological phase transition can be approximated in terms of their energy density as a function of bubble size. Bubble collisions and post-collision classical evolution negligibly change it. The dominant energy loss is particle scattering, often in the Landau--Pomeranchuk--Migdal regime. So the GW spectrum depends on the particle-physics coupling (interpolating between the `envelope' and `bulk flow' limits), on the interaction type (gauge, Yukawa, scalar quartic, ...), and on whether particle number is conserved. Finally, we consider broken global symmetries, which give a mixture of `elastic' and `inelastic' collisions.

reserve.title: All Dark Matter as Primordial Black Holes: a Gravitational-Wave Test
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36177v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a novel test for the hypothesis that the dark matter of the Universe is composed entirely by asteroidal-mass primordial black holes. It relies on detecting the stochastic gravitational-wave background generated by the coalescence onto rapidly spinning supermassive astrophysical black holes of the light primordial black holes accumulated in spherically symmetric spikes. We discuss the scenarios in which the signal can be observed by the future space-based gravitational-wave observatories LISA and DECIGO.

Its uncertainty affects the mass and radius at which the innermost stable circular orbit reaches the stellar surface, a condition that defines the transition between disks whose inner edge is set by the surface and those truncated by orbital instability. We quantify how measurements of the electric dipole polarizability of neutron-rich nuclei reduce the uncertainty in this transition and in the orbital properties at the disk inner edge. reserve.title: A Quiet Night in the Millihertz Sky? LISA Forecasts from LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA Populations
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.37617v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The high-mass black hole population inferred from ground-based observations can substantially affect the number of binaries detectable by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). We use population constraints based on data from the latest LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog (GWTC-5.0), as well as constraints from the O3 search for intermediate-mass black hole binaries, to forecast the number and masses of binary black holes detectable by LISA. reserve.title: Metric--affine gravity with dynamical chronology protection
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2604.08511v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Modified theories of gravity often introduce geometric structure beyond general relativity to address unresolved problems in the gravitational sector without invoking ad hoc matter fields. reserve.title: Minimum lifetime of a black hole
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2605.03922v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive bounds on the lifetime of an evaporating black hole. The minimum lifetime bound follows from energy conservation and purification, within the framework of `asymptotically semiclassical spacetimes'. reserve.title: Heavy Black-Holes Also Matter in Standard Siren Cosmology
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2601.03257v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: With the release of the Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog GWTC-4.0 by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) collaboration, 218 candidate detections of gravitational waves (GWs) from compact binary coalescences (CBCs) have been reported. This milestone represents a major advancement for GW cosmology, as many methods, particularly those employing the spectral siren approach, critically depend on the number of available sources. This model is designed to test the impact of heavy black holes in GW cosmology. reserve.title: The Fate of 1/4-BPS States in the D1-D5 CFT
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36057v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the 1/4-BPS operators in the D1-D5 system on AdS$_3\times S^3\times T^4$. We evaluate the anomalous dimensions of low-lying sectors in conformal perturbation theory around Sym$^N(T^4)$ exactly in $N$. All anomalous dimensions are consistent with recombination of the short multiplets into long ones and take a particularly simple form. We show that at finite $N$ and at first nontrivial order in the deformation, for the sectors we consider, the BPS density of states agrees with that of the supergravity point. To the order in conformal perturbation theory we consider, this confirms that not all states that can get lifted do get lifted.

primary.snippet: In the AI era, the biggest costs in an SoC project often come from execution, driven by hidden costs that build up when IP is sourced piece by piece from multiple vendors. This originates in reading the memoir Surely You’re Joking, Mr. Feynman as a teenager, in which Richard Feynman recounts picking locks and cracking combinations while at his day job working on the Manhattan Project at Los Alamos. reserve.title: How Much Can Semiconductor Models Hide?
reserve.snippet: Key Takeaways: Advanced packaging pushes process behavior across company lines, so what one supplier hides now shapes another company’s prediction. Encryption and abstraction protect the recipe cleanly, but neither tells the receiving engineer where the model stops being valid. A model can be accurate and still be wrong for the question asked, making its envelope as much a deliverable as the model. The goal seems simple — share the model without sharing the process. A materials supplier shouldn’t have to reveal a proprietary formulation just so a customer can predict how it will behave in a package, and a foundry shouldn’t have to hand over its recipe to provide a useful model of a chiplet. reserve.title: How particle physics stops ultra-relativistic bubbles and shapes their gravitational waves
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36160v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The gravitational-wave spectrum produced by ultra-relativistic bubbles in a first-order cosmological phase transition can be approximated in terms of their energy density as a function of bubble size. So the GW spectrum depends on the particle-physics coupling (interpolating between the `envelope' and `bulk flow' limits), on the interaction type (gauge, Yukawa, scalar quartic, ...), and on whether particle number is conserved. primary.title: How Much Can Semiconductor Models Hide?
primary.snippet: Key Takeaways: Advanced packaging pushes process behavior across company lines, so what one supplier hides now shapes another company’s prediction. Encryption and abstraction protect the recipe cleanly, but neither tells the receiving engineer where the model stops being valid. A model can be accurate and still be wrong for the question asked, making its envelope as much a deliverable as the model. The goal seems simple — share the model without sharing the process. reserve.snippet: arXiv:2601.03257v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: With the release of the Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog GWTC-4.0 by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) collaboration, 218 candidate detections of gravitational waves (GWs) from compact binary coalescences (CBCs) have been reported. This milestone represents a major advancement for GW cosmology, as many methods, particularly those employing the spectral siren approach, critically depend on the number of available sources. reserve.title: The Fate of 1/4-BPS States in the D1-D5 CFT
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36057v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the 1/4-BPS operators in the D1-D5 system on AdS$_3\times S^3\times T^4$. We evaluate the anomalous dimensions of low-lying sectors in conformal perturbation theory around Sym$^N(T^4)$ exactly in $N$. All anomalous dimensions are consistent with recombination of the short multiplets into long ones and take a particularly simple form. We show that at finite $N$ and at first nontrivial order in the deformation, for the sectors we consider, the BPS density of states agrees with that of the supergravity point. To the order in conformal perturbation theory we consider, this confirms that not all states that can get lifted do get lifted.

primary.snippet: The growing demand for high-performance computing and compact electronics has driven the transition toward advanced three-dimensional (3D) packaging technologies. primary.snippet: We study a family of fibre-cofibre sequences in the $\infty$-category of exact $\infty$-categories, which we call Keller sequences, generalising the notion of Verdier sequences of stable $\infty$-categories. We show that algebraic K-theory is localising with respect to this family, and use this to give a categorical proof of Quillen's resolution theorem. Our arguments hinge upon a mapping space characterisation of special inclusions as studied by Keller, from which we deduce another proof of Keller's theorem that such inclusions induce fully faithful functors on stable envelopes.

reserve.title: How Much Can Semiconductor Models Hide?
reserve.snippet: Key Takeaways: Advanced packaging pushes process behavior across company lines, so what one supplier hides now shapes another company’s prediction. Encryption and abstraction protect the recipe cleanly, but neither tells the receiving engineer where the model stops being valid. A model can be accurate and still be wrong for the question asked, making its envelope as much a deliverable as the model. The goal seems simple — share the model without sharing the process. A materials supplier shouldn’t have to reveal a proprietary formulation just so a customer can predict how it will behave in a package, and a foundry shouldn’t have to hand over its recipe to provide a useful model of a chiplet. reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36123v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study develops a new gauge condition for performing long duration numerical evolutions of Einstein's equation on cosmological spacetimes with non-trivial spatial topologies. This new gauge makes it possible to perform reliable numerical evolutions on these manifolds in which the spatial volumes become more than one million times larger. This new condition was tested for this study by evolving homogeneous and isotropic initial data on exemplar manifolds with three spatial topologies: Sixth-Turn space, the lens space L(5,2), and the Seifert fiber space SFS[S2:(2,1)(2,1)(2,-1)].

reserve.title: How particle physics stops ultra-relativistic bubbles and shapes their gravitational waves
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36160v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The gravitational-wave spectrum produced by ultra-relativistic bubbles in a first-order cosmological phase transition can be approximated in terms of their energy density as a function of bubble size. Bubble collisions and post-collision classical evolution negligibly change it. The dominant energy loss is particle scattering, often in the Landau--Pomeranchuk--Migdal regime. So the GW spectrum depends on the particle-physics coupling (interpolating between the `envelope' and `bulk flow' limits), on the interaction type (gauge, Yukawa, scalar quartic, ...), and on whether particle number is conserved. Finally, we consider broken global symmetries, which give a mixture of `elastic' and `inelastic' collisions.

reserve.title: All Dark Matter as Primordial Black Holes: a Gravitational-Wave Test
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36177v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a novel test for the hypothesis that the dark matter of the Universe is composed entirely by asteroidal-mass primordial black holes. It relies on detecting the stochastic gravitational-wave background generated by the coalescence onto rapidly spinning supermassive astrophysical black holes of the light primordial black holes accumulated in spherically symmetric spikes. We discuss the scenarios in which the signal can be observed by the future space-based gravitational-wave observatories LISA and DECIGO.

science.title: No off-diagonal quantum focusing for R\'enyi divergences
science.snippet: arXiv:2607.07799v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The quantum focusing conjecture (QFC) is a mathematical expression of the idea that semiclassical gravity remains universally attractive. In its non-gravitational limit, the diagonal inequality is the quantum null energy condition (QNEC), which requires convexity of relative entropy with respect to the vacuum under null deformations. R\'enyi divergences generalize relative entropy, and positive results for the diagonal R\'enyi QNEC raise the question of whether they also satisfy the off-diagonal inequalities required by a full focusing principle. We show that classical correlations between distinct null generators obstruct this extension for any non-affine R\'enyi-type divergence satisfying data processing, tensor additivity, and matched classical-quantum conditioning.

reserve.title: How Much Can Semiconductor Models Hide?
reserve.snippet: Key Takeaways: Advanced packaging pushes process behavior across company lines, so what one supplier hides now shapes another company’s prediction. Encryption and abstraction protect the recipe cleanly, but neither tells the receiving engineer where the model stops being valid. A model can be accurate and still be wrong for the question asked, making its envelope as much a deliverable as the model. The goal seems simple — share the model without sharing the process. A materials supplier shouldn’t have to reveal a proprietary formulation just so a customer can predict how it will behave in a package, and a foundry shouldn’t have to hand over its recipe to provide a useful model of a chiplet. primary.title: How Much Can Semiconductor Models Hide?
primary.snippet: Key Takeaways: Advanced packaging pushes process behavior across company lines, so what one supplier hides now shapes another company’s prediction. Encryption and abstraction protect the recipe cleanly, but neither tells the receiving engineer where the model stops being valid. A model can be accurate and still be wrong for the question asked, making its envelope as much a deliverable as the model. The goal seems simple — share the model without sharing the process. A materials supplier shouldn’t have to reveal a proprietary formulation just so a customer can predict how it will behave in a package, and a foundry shouldn’t have to hand over its recipe to provide a useful model of a chiplet. primary.title: How Much Can Semiconductor Models Hide?
primary.snippet: Key Takeaways: Advanced packaging pushes process behavior across company lines, so what one supplier hides now shapes another company’s prediction. Encryption and abstraction protect the recipe cleanly, but neither tells the receiving engineer where the model stops being valid. A model can be accurate and still be wrong for the question asked, making its envelope as much a deliverable as the model. The goal seems simple — share the model without sharing the process. A materials supplier shouldn’t have to reveal a proprietary formulation just so a customer can predict how it will behave in a package, and a foundry shouldn’t have to hand over its recipe to provide a useful model of a chiplet. reserve.title: How particle physics stops ultra-relativistic bubbles and shapes their gravitational waves
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36160v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The gravitational-wave spectrum produced by ultra-relativistic bubbles in a first-order cosmological phase transition can be approximated in terms of their energy density as a function of bubble size. primary.title: How Much Can Semiconductor Models Hide?
primary.snippet: Key Takeaways: Advanced packaging pushes process behavior across company lines, so what one supplier hides now shapes another company’s prediction. Encryption and abstraction protect the recipe cleanly, but neither tells the receiving engineer where the model stops being valid. reserve.title: How particle physics stops ultra-relativistic bubbles and shapes their gravitational waves
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36160v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The gravitational-wave spectrum produced by ultra-relativistic bubbles in a first-order cosmological phase transition can be approximated in terms of their energy density as a function of bubble size. We further introduce a small perturbation in one of the K\"{a}hler moduli that modifies the existing potential in the field space. The effective correction in the moduli space is made by introducing a localised Gaussian bump, which induces an ultra-slow-roll feature in the inflaton potential during the early cosmological inflation. reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate a description of self-gravitating Schr\"odinger--Poisson (SP) solitons in curved spacetime using a local inertial frame centered on the soliton. In the weak-field and non-relativistic regime, the effect of the background spacetime is incorporated into the SP equations through an effective tidal potential determined by the spacetime curvature. We apply this framework to a soliton moving along a circular equatorial geodesic around a Kerr black hole. The tidal field contains stationary and time-dependent quadrupolar components, which induce a deformation of the soliton and an associated mass quadrupole moment. We formulate the quadrupolar response in terms of the tidal deformability and the dimensionless Love number. reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.37331v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we investigate the geodesic dynamics and tidal force effects in neutral and electrically charged regular spacetimes inspired by T-duality. reserve.title: One Method to Find Them All: Analytic Black Holes beyond Einstein
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.37515v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rotating black holes offer powerful probes of gravity, but constructing their geometries beyond vacuum general relativity remains challenging. reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.37525v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate how deviations from the Schwarzschild geometry affect the motion of massive test particles and the gravitational radiation associated with their periodic trajectories around a new improved Schwarzschild black hole. reserve.title: Weighing dark matter particles with gravitational waves
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.37638v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is commonly assumed that the mass of dark matter particles cannot be determined from their gravitational effects when dark matter behaves as collisionless matter. Here we show that extreme-mass-ratio inspirals observable by millihertz gravitational-wave observatories such as the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) could measure the mass of ultralight dark matter particles in sufficiently dense dark matter spikes. The separation of scales between the two black holes allows ultralight dark matter to form a collisionless density spike around the massive primary while retaining wave effects in its interaction with the stellar-mass companion. reserve.title: How particle physics stops ultra-relativistic bubbles and shapes their gravitational waves
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36160v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The gravitational-wave spectrum produced by ultra-relativistic bubbles in a first-order cosmological phase transition can be approximated in terms of their energy density as a function of bubble size. Bubble collisions and post-collision classical evolution negligibly change it. The dominant energy loss is particle scattering, often in the Landau--Pomeranchuk--Migdal regime. So the GW spectrum depends on the particle-physics coupling (interpolating between the `envelope' and `bulk flow' limits), on the interaction type (gauge, Yukawa, scalar quartic, ...), and on whether particle number is conserved. Finally, we consider broken global symmetries, which give a mixture of `elastic' and `inelastic' collisions.

reserve.title: All Dark Matter as Primordial Black Holes: a Gravitational-Wave Test
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36177v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a novel test for the hypothesis that the dark matter of the Universe is composed entirely by asteroidal-mass primordial black holes. It relies on detecting the stochastic gravitational-wave background generated by the coalescence onto rapidly spinning supermassive astrophysical black holes of the light primordial black holes accumulated in spherically symmetric spikes. We discuss the scenarios in which the signal can be observed by the future space-based gravitational-wave observatories LISA and DECIGO.

We quantify how measurements of the electric dipole polarizability of neutron-rich nuclei reduce the uncertainty in this transition and in the orbital properties at the disk inner edge. reserve.title: Metric--affine gravity with dynamical chronology protection
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2604.08511v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Modified theories of gravity often introduce geometric structure beyond general relativity to address unresolved problems in the gravitational sector without invoking ad hoc matter fields. reserve.title: Minimum lifetime of a black hole

reserve.title: Heavy Black-Holes Also Matter in Standard Siren Cosmology
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2601.03257v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: With the release of the Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog GWTC-4.0 by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) collaboration, 218 candidate detections of gravitational waves (GWs) from compact binary coalescences (CBCs) have been reported. This milestone represents a major advancement for GW cosmology, as many methods, particularly those employing the spectral siren approach, critically depend on the number of available sources. We investigate the impact of a novel parametric model describing the full population mass spectrum of CBCs on the estimation of the Hubble constant. This model is designed to test the impact of heavy black holes in GW cosmology. reserve.title: The Fate of 1/4-BPS States in the D1-D5 CFT
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36057v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the 1/4-BPS operators in the D1-D5 system on AdS$_3\times S^3\times T^4$. We evaluate the anomalous dimensions of low-lying sectors in conformal perturbation theory around Sym$^N(T^4)$ exactly in $N$. All anomalous dimensions are consistent with recombination of the short multiplets into long ones and take a particularly simple form. We show that at finite $N$ and at first nontrivial order in the deformation, for the sectors we consider, the BPS density of states agrees with that of the supergravity point. To the order in conformal perturbation theory we consider, this confirms that not all states that can get lifted do get lifted.

primary.title: P2P: Cross-View Population Denoising for Unpaired Single-Cell Perturbation Response Prediction
primary.snippet: AIVC (AI Virtual Cell) is a learned simulator of cellular behavior across conditions. Predicting how a cell population responds transcriptionally to a genetic perturbation is a core task. Perturb-seq records that response by destructive sequencing, so a control cell and a perturbed cell are never observed as a pair, and cells under one condition remain heterogeneous and noisy. Regression on individual cells absorbs sampling variation into the estimated effect, whereas interpretation requires the reproducible population effect. P2P (Perturbation-to-Perturbation) takes a stochastic cell-set view as its supervision unit. Two views drawn from the same condition share a reproducible population effect and differ by view-specific variation. primary.snippet: The growing demand for high-performance computing and compact electronics has driven the transition toward advanced three-dimensional (3D) packaging technologies. Traditional packaging technologies, such as micro-bump interconnections, face limitations in achieving sub-micrometer pitches, prompting the development of alternative bonding strategies. primary.snippet: arXiv:2610.35935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Video on SPI-attached microcontroller displays is limited less by decoding than by where each byte lives and which stages run serially. We present RV565, a decode framework for frame-independent video whose decoded representation is the panel's native RGB565 format, and evaluate it on an ESP32-S3 with two ten-second windows of an openly licensed film. A serial path - inflate, then scale into internal-memory stripes overlapped with SPI direct-memory-access (DMA) transfers - meets the 41.7 ms deadline on the lighter window but misses all 7,200 frames of the heavier one. RV565's dual-core pipeline inflates the next frame on the second core during the transfer and sustains 24 FPS with zero misses and 10.3 ms of slack on both windows; frame time then equals the display transfer, which runs at 98.1% of the 40 MHz wire-time bound. science.title: Build a Hidden Lock With a Magnetic Imager
science.snippet: Like many a nerd, I have a certain fascination with locks. This originates in reading the memoir Surely You’re Joking, Mr. Feynman as a teenager, in which Richard Feynman recounts picking locks and cracking combinations while at his day job working on the Manhattan Project at Los Alamos. I currently have a couple of locksport pick sets and training locks that I purchased at hacker conferences over the years (although I’m still terrible at it), and I delight in the YouTube exploits of folks like the LockPickingLawyer . science.snippet: arXiv:2610.22485v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We discuss the continuum two-dimensional conformal field theory, whose target space is a two-torus. science.title: A gaussian-process reconstruction of gravitational-wave friction from dark standard sirens
science.snippet: arXiv:2610.36087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Standard sirens provide a direct probe of the cosmic distance-redshift relation and therefore a powerful test of whether gravitational waves (GWs) propagate as predicted by general relativity on cosmological scales. In many extensions of general relativity, GW propagation is modified by an anomalous friction term, which alters the amplitude evolution and leads to a GW luminosity distance that differs from its electromagnetic counterpart. science.title: Hardware-Matched Spiking Neural Networks for Real-Time Purkinje Cell Spike Classification
science.snippet: arXiv:2610.37104v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distinguishing Purkinje cell (PC) simple spikes (SSs) from complex spikes (CSs) is key to studying cerebellar function. PC recordings commonly rely on wired headstages, whose tethers restrict natural movement in freely behaving animals. Untethered headstages remove this constraint, but cannot continuously transmit raw recordings within their power budgets, making on-headstage spike classification an attractive form of compression, provided it runs accurately in real time on constrained hardware. reserve.title: How Much Can Semiconductor Models Hide?
reserve.snippet: Key Takeaways: Advanced packaging pushes process behavior across company lines, so what one supplier hides now shapes another company’s prediction. Encryption and abstraction protect the recipe cleanly, but neither tells the receiving engineer where the model stops being valid. A model can be accurate and still be wrong for the question asked, making its envelope as much a deliverable as the model. The goal seems simple — share the model without sharing the process. A materials supplier shouldn’t have to reveal a proprietary formulation just so a customer can predict how it will behave in a package, and a foundry shouldn’t have to hand over its recipe to provide a useful model of a chiplet. reserve.title: Improved Gauge Conditions for Large Expansion Cosmological Models
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36123v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study develops a new gauge condition for performing long duration numerical evolutions of Einstein's equation on cosmological spacetimes with non-trivial spatial topologies. This new gauge makes it possible to perform reliable numerical evolutions on these manifolds in which the spatial volumes become more than one million times larger. This new condition was tested for this study by evolving homogeneous and isotropic initial data on exemplar manifolds with three spatial topologies: Sixth-Turn space, the lens space L(5,2), and the Seifert fiber space SFS[S2:(2,1)(2,1)(2,-1)].

We further introduce a small perturbation in one of the K\"{a}hler moduli that modifies the existing potential in the field space. The effective correction in the moduli space is made by introducing a localised Gaussian bump, which induces an ultra-slow-roll feature in the inflaton potential during the early cosmological inflation. The evolution of the amplitude of the curvature power spectrum is solved numerically by using the Mukhanov-Sasaki equation, with Bunch-Davies initial conditions. reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate a description of self-gravitating Schr\"odinger--Poisson (SP) solitons in curved spacetime using a local inertial frame centered on the soliton. In the weak-field and non-relativistic regime, the effect of the background spacetime is incorporated into the SP equations through an effective tidal potential determined by the spacetime curvature. We apply this framework to a soliton moving along a circular equatorial geodesic around a Kerr black hole. The tidal field contains stationary and time-dependent quadrupolar components, which induce a deformation of the soliton and an associated mass quadrupole moment. We formulate the quadrupolar response in terms of the tidal deformability and the dimensionless Love number. reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.37331v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we investigate the geodesic dynamics and tidal force effects in neutral and electrically charged regular spacetimes inspired by T-duality. We first analyze the geometric properties of these solutions, including their regular central structure and horizon configurations, and show how the interplay between the T-duality scale $\ell_0$ and the electric charge $Q$ determines the transition between black hole and horizonless geometries. We then study the motion of massive and massless particles through the corresponding effective potentials, examining the existence and stability of circular orbits and the behavior of their characteristic radii. reserve.title: One Method to Find Them All: Analytic Black Holes beyond Einstein
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.37515v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rotating black holes offer powerful probes of gravity, but constructing their geometries beyond vacuum general relativity remains challenging. reserve.title: Weighing dark matter particles with gravitational waves
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.37638v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is commonly assumed that the mass of dark matter particles cannot be determined from their gravitational effects when dark matter behaves as collisionless matter. Here we show that extreme-mass-ratio inspirals observable by millihertz gravitational-wave observatories such as the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) could measure the mass of ultralight dark matter particles in sufficiently dense dark matter spikes. The separation of scales between the two black holes allows ultralight dark matter to form a collisionless density spike around the massive primary while retaining wave effects in its interaction with the stellar-mass companion. reserve.title: How particle physics stops ultra-relativistic bubbles and shapes their gravitational waves
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36160v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The gravitational-wave spectrum produced by ultra-relativistic bubbles in a first-order cosmological phase transition can be approximated in terms of their energy density as a function of bubble size. Bubble collisions and post-collision classical evolution negligibly change it. The dominant energy loss is particle scattering, often in the Landau--Pomeranchuk--Migdal regime. So the GW spectrum depends on the particle-physics coupling (interpolating between the `envelope' and `bulk flow' limits), on the interaction type (gauge, Yukawa, scalar quartic, ...), and on whether particle number is conserved. Finally, we consider broken global symmetries, which give a mixture of `elastic' and `inelastic' collisions.

reserve.title: All Dark Matter as Primordial Black Holes: a Gravitational-Wave Test
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36177v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a novel test for the hypothesis that the dark matter of the Universe is composed entirely by asteroidal-mass primordial black holes. It relies on detecting the stochastic gravitational-wave background generated by the coalescence onto rapidly spinning supermassive astrophysical black holes of the light primordial black holes accumulated in spherically symmetric spikes. We discuss the scenarios in which the signal can be observed by the future space-based gravitational-wave observatories LISA and DECIGO.

We quantify how measurements of the electric dipole polarizability of neutron-rich nuclei reduce the uncertainty in this transition and in the orbital properties at the disk inner edge. reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.37617v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The high-mass black hole population inferred from ground-based observations can substantially affect the number of binaries detectable by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). reserve.snippet: arXiv:2604.08511v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Modified theories of gravity often introduce geometric structure beyond general relativity to address unresolved problems in the gravitational sector without invoking ad hoc matter fields. Although chronology protection was not the original motivation for either theory, both can realize it classically through stable causality. reserve.title: Minimum lifetime of a black hole
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2605.03922v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive bounds on the lifetime of an evaporating black hole. The minimum lifetime bound follows from energy conservation and purification, within the framework of `asymptotically semiclassical spacetimes'. We discuss the energy-cost of entanglement purification and find a lower bound on the purification time of the black hole, which scales as $M_0^4/\hbar^{3/2}$, where $M_0$ is the initial black hole mass. reserve.title: Heavy Black-Holes Also Matter in Standard Siren Cosmology
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2601.03257v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: With the release of the Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog GWTC-4.0 by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) collaboration, 218 candidate detections of gravitational waves (GWs) from compact binary coalescences (CBCs) have been reported. This milestone represents a major advancement for GW cosmology, as many methods, particularly those employing the spectral siren approach, critically depend on the number of available sources. We investigate the impact of a novel parametric model describing the full population mass spectrum of CBCs on the estimation of the Hubble constant. This model is designed to test the impact of heavy black holes in GW cosmology. reserve.title: The Fate of 1/4-BPS States in the D1-D5 CFT
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36057v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the 1/4-BPS operators in the D1-D5 system on AdS$_3\times S^3\times T^4$. We evaluate the anomalous dimensions of low-lying sectors in conformal perturbation theory around Sym$^N(T^4)$ exactly in $N$. All anomalous dimensions are consistent with recombination of the short multiplets into long ones and take a particularly simple form. We show that at finite $N$ and at first nontrivial order in the deformation, for the sectors we consider, the BPS density of states agrees with that of the supergravity point. To the order in conformal perturbation theory we consider, this confirms that not all states that can get lifted do get lifted.

reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.33134v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Beyond math and code, Large language models (LLMs) are beginning to tackle problems that have traditionally required substantial training for theoretical physicists, but it remains unclear how far this capability extends and where it might break. As a first step toward pushing LLMs in high-energy theoretical physics, we introduce QFT-Bench, a benchmark of 75 graduate- to research-level problems requiring extensive reasoning and derivation across core Quantum Field Theory (QFT) subareas. Each question has a well-defined target and closed-form reference answer. Evaluation combines symbolic verification with LLM-based judge. reserve.title: The Harmonic Structure of Multiparticle Scattering: Amplitude Projection and Non-Renormalization
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36052v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a projection formalism for four-dimensional massless scattering amplitudes based on the construction of harmonics on multi-particle phase space. This provides a generalization of the partial-wave decomposition valid for any number of particles. Applying this formalism to calculations of on-shell cuts, we show that any cut calculation can be rewritten as a sum of products of projected coefficients and derive a condition for this sum to vanish. Using the on-shell renormalization group equation in combination with our projection formalism, we derive new non-renormalization theorems for effective field theories valid at general loop orders.

primary.title: RV565: Cross-Layer Co-Design for Frame-Independent Video Playback on MicroPython-Class ESP32-S3 Systems
primary.snippet: arXiv:2610.35935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Video on SPI-attached microcontroller displays is limited less by decoding than by where each byte lives and which stages run serially. We present RV565, a decode framework for frame-independent video whose decoded representation is the panel's native RGB565 format, and evaluate it on an ESP32-S3 with two ten-second windows of an openly licensed film. A serial path - inflate, then scale into internal-memory stripes overlapped with SPI direct-memory-access (DMA) transfers - meets the 41.7 ms deadline on the lighter window but misses all 7,200 frames of the heavier one. RV565's dual-core pipeline inflates the next frame on the second core during the transfer and sustains 24 FPS with zero misses and 10.3 ms of slack on both windows; frame time then equals the display transfer, which runs at 98.1% of the 40 MHz wire-time bound. primary.title: VIPER: Architecture-Aware Performance Modeling for Processing-in-Memory Design-Space Exploration
primary.snippet: Processing-in-Memory (PIM) promises to reduce data movement overhead by executing computation in or near memory, but its realized application speedup remains highly design-dependent. Non-offloadable host execution, host-PIM transfers, limited PIM capacity, and device programming latency can limit end-to-end speedup, making fast early-stage design-space exploration (DSE) essential. However, existing PIM evaluation methods remain limited: circuit- and device-level tools cannot capture these end-to-end PIM performance factors, while cycle-accurate simulation is too slow for iterative DSE. To address this gap, we present VIPER, a unified, lightweight, and architecture-aware performance evaluation framework for PIM DSE. primary.snippet: The growing demand for high-performance computing and compact electronics has driven the transition toward advanced three-dimensional (3D) packaging technologies. science.title: Build a Hidden Lock With a Magnetic Imager
science.snippet: Like many a nerd, I have a certain fascination with locks. This originates in reading the memoir Surely You’re Joking, Mr. Feynman as a teenager, in which Richard Feynman recounts picking locks and cracking combinations while at his day job working on the Manhattan Project at Los Alamos. I currently have a couple of locksport pick sets and training locks that I purchased at hacker conferences over the years (although I’m still terrible at it), and I delight in the YouTube exploits of folks like the LockPickingLawyer . science.snippet: arXiv:2610.36087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Standard sirens provide a direct probe of the cosmic distance-redshift relation and therefore a powerful test of whether gravitational waves (GWs) propagate as predicted by general relativity on cosmological scales. reserve.title: Hardware-Matched Spiking Neural Networks for Real-Time Purkinje Cell Spike Classification
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.37104v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distinguishing Purkinje cell (PC) simple spikes (SSs) from complex spikes (CSs) is key to studying cerebellar function. PC recordings commonly rely on wired headstages, whose tethers restrict natural movement in freely behaving animals. reserve.title: How Much Can Semiconductor Models Hide?
reserve.snippet: Key Takeaways: Advanced packaging pushes process behavior across company lines, so what one supplier hides now shapes another company’s prediction. Encryption and abstraction protect the recipe cleanly, but neither tells the receiving engineer where the model stops being valid. A model can be accurate and still be wrong for the question asked, making its envelope as much a deliverable as the model. The goal seems simple — share the model without sharing the process. A materials supplier shouldn’t have to reveal a proprietary formulation just so a customer can predict how it will behave in a package, and a foundry shouldn’t have to hand over its recipe to provide a useful model of a chiplet. reserve.title: Improved Gauge Conditions for Large Expansion Cosmological Models
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36123v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study develops a new gauge condition for performing long duration numerical evolutions of Einstein's equation on cosmological spacetimes with non-trivial spatial topologies. This new gauge makes it possible to perform reliable numerical evolutions on these manifolds in which the spatial volumes become more than one million times larger. This new condition was tested for this study by evolving homogeneous and isotropic initial data on exemplar manifolds with three spatial topologies: Sixth-Turn space, the lens space L(5,2), and the Seifert fiber space SFS[S2:(2,1)(2,1)(2,-1)].

reserve.title: Weighing dark matter particles with gravitational waves
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.37638v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is commonly assumed that the mass of dark matter particles cannot be determined from their gravitational effects when dark matter behaves as collisionless matter. Here we show that extreme-mass-ratio inspirals observable by millihertz gravitational-wave observatories such as the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) could measure the mass of ultralight dark matter particles in sufficiently dense dark matter spikes. The separation of scales between the two black holes allows ultralight dark matter to form a collisionless density spike around the massive primary while retaining wave effects in its interaction with the stellar-mass companion. reserve.title: How particle physics stops ultra-relativistic bubbles and shapes their gravitational waves
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36160v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The gravitational-wave spectrum produced by ultra-relativistic bubbles in a first-order cosmological phase transition can be approximated in terms of their energy density as a function of bubble size. Bubble collisions and post-collision classical evolution negligibly change it. The dominant energy loss is particle scattering, often in the Landau--Pomeranchuk--Migdal regime. So the GW spectrum depends on the particle-physics coupling (interpolating between the `envelope' and `bulk flow' limits), on the interaction type (gauge, Yukawa, scalar quartic, ...), and on whether particle number is conserved. Finally, we consider broken global symmetries, which give a mixture of `elastic' and `inelastic' collisions.

reserve.title: All Dark Matter as Primordial Black Holes: a Gravitational-Wave Test
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36177v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a novel test for the hypothesis that the dark matter of the Universe is composed entirely by asteroidal-mass primordial black holes. It relies on detecting the stochastic gravitational-wave background generated by the coalescence onto rapidly spinning supermassive astrophysical black holes of the light primordial black holes accumulated in spherically symmetric spikes. We discuss the scenarios in which the signal can be observed by the future space-based gravitational-wave observatories LISA and DECIGO.

reserve.snippet: arXiv:2604.08511v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Modified theories of gravity often introduce geometric structure beyond general relativity to address unresolved problems in the gravitational sector without invoking ad hoc matter fields. reserve.title: Heavy Black-Holes Also Matter in Standard Siren Cosmology
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2601.03257v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: With the release of the Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog GWTC-4.0 by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) collaboration, 218 candidate detections of gravitational waves (GWs) from compact binary coalescences (CBCs) have been reported. reserve.title: The Fate of 1/4-BPS States in the D1-D5 CFT
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36057v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the 1/4-BPS operators in the D1-D5 system on AdS$_3\times S^3\times T^4$. We evaluate the anomalous dimensions of low-lying sectors in conformal perturbation theory around Sym$^N(T^4)$ exactly in $N$. All anomalous dimensions are consistent with recombination of the short multiplets into long ones and take a particularly simple form. We show that at finite $N$ and at first nontrivial order in the deformation, for the sectors we consider, the BPS density of states agrees with that of the supergravity point. To the order in conformal perturbation theory we consider, this confirms that not all states that can get lifted do get lifted.

primary.snippet: arXiv:2610.35935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Video on SPI-attached microcontroller displays is limited less by decoding than by where each byte lives and which stages run serially. We present RV565, a decode framework for frame-independent video whose decoded representation is the panel's native RGB565 format, and evaluate it on an ESP32-S3 with two ten-second windows of an openly licensed film. A serial path - inflate, then scale into internal-memory stripes overlapped with SPI direct-memory-access (DMA) transfers - meets the 41.7 ms deadline on the lighter window but misses all 7,200 frames of the heavier one. RV565's dual-core pipeline inflates the next frame on the second core during the transfer and sustains 24 FPS with zero misses and 10.3 ms of slack on both windows; frame time then equals the display transfer, which runs at 98.1% of the 40 MHz wire-time bound. primary.title: How Much Can Semiconductor Models Hide?
primary.snippet: Key Takeaways: Advanced packaging pushes process behavior across company lines, so what one supplier hides now shapes another company’s prediction. Encryption and abstraction protect the recipe cleanly, but neither tells the receiving engineer where the model stops being valid. A model can be accurate and still be wrong for the question asked, making its envelope as much a deliverable as the model. The goal seems simple — share the model without sharing the process. A materials supplier shouldn’t have to reveal a proprietary formulation just so a customer can predict how it will behave in a package, and a foundry shouldn’t have to hand over its recipe to provide a useful model of a chiplet. But advanced packaging is making that separation much harder to maintain. primary.title: Foundation IP For The AI Era: Why Execution Saves You Millions On HPC And Edge AI SoCs
primary.snippet: In the AI era, the biggest costs in an SoC project often come from execution, driven by hidden costs that build up when IP is sourced piece by piece from multiple vendors. At advanced nodes, re-spins, integration delays and missed tape-out dates can put millions of dollars at risk. This eBook explains how a single, integrated Foundation IP platform reduces that risk and helps lower TCO. The solution includes silicon-proven logic libraries, embedded memories, IOs and NVM, and it’s backed by IP + EDA co-optimization and one support team. Using modeled examples from HPC and Edge AI SoCs, it shows how predictable execution can lead to significant savings, from avoided re-spins and schedule slips to measurable power, performance and area (PPA) gains. science.snippet: Two-dimensional (2D) materials have attracted a lot of attention in recent years for their excellent electronic, thermal and mechanical properties, as well as their interesting quantum effects. science.title: Quantum field theory and four-manifolds: Perspectives from physics and geometry
science.snippet: arXiv:2610.30288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: These lecture notes are based on lecture series by the authors for the Summer School 2025 on ``Physical mathematics of quantum field theory" at the University of Massachusetts Amherst organized by Owen Gwilliam, Chris Elliott, and Matteo Lotito. science.snippet: arXiv:2610.37104v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distinguishing Purkinje cell (PC) simple spikes (SSs) from complex spikes (CSs) is key to studying cerebellar function. reserve.title: How particle physics stops ultra-relativistic bubbles and shapes their gravitational waves
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36160v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The gravitational-wave spectrum produced by ultra-relativistic bubbles in a first-order cosmological phase transition can be approximated in terms of their energy density as a function of bubble size. reserve.title: How Much Can Semiconductor Models Hide?
reserve.snippet: Key Takeaways: Advanced packaging pushes process behavior across company lines, so what one supplier hides now shapes another company’s prediction. science.snippet: arXiv:2610.34455v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The flip tilt illusion is the misperception of the orientation of the alignment between a pair of dots by 90 degrees. science.title: A gaussian-process reconstruction of gravitational-wave friction from dark standard sirens
science.snippet: arXiv:2610.36087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Standard sirens provide a direct probe of the cosmic distance-redshift relation and therefore a powerful test of whether gravitational waves (GWs) propagate as predicted by general relativity on cosmological scales. reserve.title: Hardware-Matched Spiking Neural Networks for Real-Time Purkinje Cell Spike Classification
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.37104v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distinguishing Purkinje cell (PC) simple spikes (SSs) from complex spikes (CSs) is key to studying cerebellar function. PC recordings commonly rely on wired headstages, whose tethers restrict natural movement in freely behaving animals. Untethered headstages remove this constraint, but cannot continuously transmit raw recordings within their power budgets, making on-headstage spike classification an attractive form of compression, provided it runs accurately in real time on constrained hardware. reserve.title: Improved Gauge Conditions for Large Expansion Cosmological Models
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36123v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study develops a new gauge condition for performing long duration numerical evolutions of Einstein's equation on cosmological spacetimes with non-trivial spatial topologies. This new gauge makes it possible to perform reliable numerical evolutions on these manifolds in which the spatial volumes become more than one million times larger. This new condition was tested for this study by evolving homogeneous and isotropic initial data on exemplar manifolds with three spatial topologies: Sixth-Turn space, the lens space L(5,2), and the Seifert fiber space SFS[S2:(2,1)(2,1)(2,-1)].

reserve.title: Weighing dark matter particles with gravitational waves
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.37638v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is commonly assumed that the mass of dark matter particles cannot be determined from their gravitational effects when dark matter behaves as collisionless matter. Here we show that extreme-mass-ratio inspirals observable by millihertz gravitational-wave observatories such as the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) could measure the mass of ultralight dark matter particles in sufficiently dense dark matter spikes. The separation of scales between the two black holes allows ultralight dark matter to form a collisionless density spike around the massive primary while retaining wave effects in its interaction with the stellar-mass companion. reserve.title: How particle physics stops ultra-relativistic bubbles and shapes their gravitational waves
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36160v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The gravitational-wave spectrum produced by ultra-relativistic bubbles in a first-order cosmological phase transition can be approximated in terms of their energy density as a function of bubble size. Bubble collisions and post-collision classical evolution negligibly change it. The dominant energy loss is particle scattering, often in the Landau--Pomeranchuk--Migdal regime. So the GW spectrum depends on the particle-physics coupling (interpolating between the `envelope' and `bulk flow' limits), on the interaction type (gauge, Yukawa, scalar quartic, ...), and on whether particle number is conserved. Finally, we consider broken global symmetries, which give a mixture of `elastic' and `inelastic' collisions.

reserve.title: All Dark Matter as Primordial Black Holes: a Gravitational-Wave Test
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36177v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a novel test for the hypothesis that the dark matter of the Universe is composed entirely by asteroidal-mass primordial black holes. It relies on detecting the stochastic gravitational-wave background generated by the coalescence onto rapidly spinning supermassive astrophysical black holes of the light primordial black holes accumulated in spherically symmetric spikes. We discuss the scenarios in which the signal can be observed by the future space-based gravitational-wave observatories LISA and DECIGO.

reserve.title: Minimum lifetime of a black hole

reserve.title: Heavy Black-Holes Also Matter in Standard Siren Cosmology
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2601.03257v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: With the release of the Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog GWTC-4.0 by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) collaboration, 218 candidate detections of gravitational waves (GWs) from compact binary coalescences (CBCs) have been reported. This milestone represents a major advancement for GW cosmology, as many methods, particularly those employing the spectral siren approach, critically depend on the number of available sources. We investigate the impact of a novel parametric model describing the full population mass spectrum of CBCs on the estimation of the Hubble constant. This model is designed to test the impact of heavy black holes in GW cosmology. reserve.title: The Fate of 1/4-BPS States in the D1-D5 CFT
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36057v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the 1/4-BPS operators in the D1-D5 system on AdS$_3\times S^3\times T^4$. We evaluate the anomalous dimensions of low-lying sectors in conformal perturbation theory around Sym$^N(T^4)$ exactly in $N$. All anomalous dimensions are consistent with recombination of the short multiplets into long ones and take a particularly simple form. We show that at finite $N$ and at first nontrivial order in the deformation, for the sectors we consider, the BPS density of states agrees with that of the supergravity point. To the order in conformal perturbation theory we consider, this confirms that not all states that can get lifted do get lifted.

primary.snippet: arXiv:2610.23767v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern GPU compilers expose rich layout abstractions for mapping tensors to threads and on-chip resources, but compute-unit-local (CU-local) 3D DRAM architectures lack a corresponding abstraction for specifying how operand-tile data are arranged within the DRAM address space. science.title: Edge AI for Smart Cities: From Insight to Cognitive Action
science.snippet: This white paper explains how edge AI and physical AI help cities move beyond passive monitoring. It shows how urban infrastructure can sense, reason, and act on real-time conditions across public safety, mobility, and infrastructure management. What you will learn about: How the shift from smart cities to cognitive cities depends on infrastructure that reasons and acts, rather than infrastructure that only monitors. science.snippet: arXiv:2610.36057v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the 1/4-BPS operators in the D1-D5 system on AdS$_3\times S^3\times T^4$. This originates in reading the memoir Surely You’re Joking, Mr. Feynman as a teenager, in which Richard Feynman recounts picking locks and cracking combinations while at his day job working on the Manhattan Project at Los Alamos. I currently have a couple of locksport pick sets and training locks that I purchased at hacker conferences over the years (although I’m still terrible at it), and I delight in the YouTube exploits of folks like the LockPickingLawyer . All of which left me wondering if I could try building an interesting lock. One dodge that lockmakers have long used to challenge would-be plunderers is to conceal the existence of the lock itself. science.title: A gaussian-process reconstruction of gravitational-wave friction from dark standard sirens
science.snippet: arXiv:2610.36087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Standard sirens provide a direct probe of the cosmic distance-redshift relation and therefore a powerful test of whether gravitational waves (GWs) propagate as predicted by general relativity on cosmological scales. In many extensions of general relativity, GW propagation is modified by an anomalous friction term, which alters the amplitude evolution and leads to a GW luminosity distance that differs from its electromagnetic counterpart. In this work, we develop a non-parametric reconstruction of this anomalous friction from dark standard sirens. science.title: Hardware-Matched Spiking Neural Networks for Real-Time Purkinje Cell Spike Classification
science.snippet: arXiv:2610.37104v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distinguishing Purkinje cell (PC) simple spikes (SSs) from complex spikes (CSs) is key to studying cerebellar function. PC recordings commonly rely on wired headstages, whose tethers restrict natural movement in freely behaving animals. Untethered headstages remove this constraint, but cannot continuously transmit raw recordings within their power budgets, making on-headstage spike classification an attractive form of compression, provided it runs accurately in real time on constrained hardware. This work presents two compact spiking neural networks (SNNs) matched to their target hardware: ConvSNN, which maps to the Matrix Vector Processor (MVP) of an EFM32PG28 microcontroller, and StreamSNN, which processes one waveform value per timestep using learned time constants and fixed synaptic delays for a dedicated SKY130 circuit. science.title: Soft scalar-field corrections to the topological susceptibility
science.snippet: arXiv:2610.31756v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute the contribution from soft scalar-field fluctuations to the topological susceptibility in SU(2) gauge theory at high temperature. We construct a 3-dimensional effective theory for the scalar field that accounts for the presence of an instanton. In the limit that the scalar selfcoupling $ \lambda $ is much larger than the square of the gauge coupling $g$ we obtain a correction of order $\sqrt{\lambda}$ relative to the 1-loop result for the topological susceptibility.

science.title: Improved Gauge Conditions for Large Expansion Cosmological Models
science.snippet: arXiv:2610.36123v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study develops a new gauge condition for performing long duration numerical evolutions of Einstein's equation on cosmological spacetimes with non-trivial spatial topologies. This new gauge makes it possible to perform reliable numerical evolutions on these manifolds in which the spatial volumes become more than one million times larger. This new condition was tested for this study by evolving homogeneous and isotropic initial data on exemplar manifolds with three spatial topologies: Sixth-Turn space, the lens space L(5,2), and the Seifert fiber space SFS[S2:(2,1)(2,1)(2,-1)].

reserve.title: Serotonin signaling enhances phagocytosis by brain macrophages through Htr2b and alleviates brain injury after stroke
reserve.snippet: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02482-y The serotonin receptor Htr2b activation enhances lysosome biogenesis and phagocytic clearance of debris to mitigate neuroinflammation and brain injury after stroke. The study proposes a potential monocyte-derived macrophage-targeted immune therapy to improve neurological outcomes after ischemic stroke.

reserve.title: How Much Can Semiconductor Models Hide?
reserve.snippet: Key Takeaways: Advanced packaging pushes process behavior across company lines, so what one supplier hides now shapes another company’s prediction. Encryption and abstraction protect the recipe cleanly, but neither tells the receiving engineer where the model stops being valid. A model can be accurate and still be wrong for the question asked, making its envelope as much a deliverable as the model. The goal seems simple — share the model without sharing the process. A materials supplier shouldn’t have to reveal a proprietary formulation just so a customer can predict how it will behave in a package, and a foundry shouldn’t have to hand over its recipe to provide a useful model of a chiplet. reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the shadows of a charged rotating de Sitter solution in fourth order conformal Weyl gravity (CWG) immersed in plasma and analyze the joint charge-plasma constraints. Our main goal is to distinguish observational effects caused by the dispersive plasma environment from those caused by the underlying gravitational theory. Within a separable Hamilton-Jacobi plasma model, we derive the radial and angular photon potentials, the equatorial finite-distance deflection angle, and the finite-observer shadow boundary due to the asymptotically non-flat nature of the CWG spacetime. reserve.title: Improved constraints on higher-derivative effective field theory extensions of general relativity with GW230627_015337
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36728v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gravitational-wave (GW) observations of binary black holes provide a powerful probe of general relativity (GR) in the strong-field regime. In effective field theory (EFT) extensions of GR, higher-curvature operators modify the binary dynamics and introduce corrections to the inspiral phase. In this work, we consider two parity-even cubic-curvature couplings and one quartic-curvature coupling, whose leading phase corrections enter at 5PN, 6PN, and 8PN order, respectively. We incorporate these corrections into the individual multipoles of the \texttt{SEOBNRv5HM\_ROM} waveform using the flexible theory-independent framework, allowing higher-order modes and the full inspiral-merger-ringdown signal to be used in the analysis. reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the greybody factor and Joule-Thomson expansion of deformed Schwarzschild-AdS black hole models. We constructed the Klein-Gordon equation into a Schr\"odinger-like wave equation using tortoise coordinates and derived the exact effective potential. Also, we analyzed its behavior under varying physical parameters, including deformation parameters, mass and angular momentum. In this case, our results illustrate that increasing the deformation parameter enhances the effective potential, significantly impacting the absorption and scattering of massless scalar fields. It is noted that the Schwarzschild black hole effective potential is greatly increased when the deformation parameter is present.
